cards.explanation: The answer is True. Her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had shown Elizabeth, the baby's mother, great mercy, and they rejoiced with her. I think that's how you treat a friend's good news. You show up and you celebrate like it happened to you.

The answer is father. The text says they were going to name him after his father Zechariah. That was the plan walking in, friends. Zechariah is the baby's dad, and the name was already sitting there like a cookie waiting on a cooling rack. Plans can change fast, though.

The answer is False. When they were going to name him Zechariah, his mother Elizabeth replied, “No! He shall be called John.” She starts with “No!” and then gives the name. I'd say she'd made up her mind.
The answer is John. After her “No!” Elizabeth says, “He shall be called John.” The text gives just the name. That's the name in verse 60.

The answer is that none of her relatives has that name. The people there tell her, “There is no one among your relatives who bears this name.” That's what they point out about John. It's about her relatives, and that's all they say here.

The answer is tablet. Zechariah asks for a tablet and writes his answer. He can't speak, so writing is how he gets it across. I went quiet for a long stretch in the back of a junk drawer, friends, and a tablet would've been handy. It's a little slower than talking, but it gets the job done.
The answer is True. Zechariah writes, “His name is John.” That's the same name Elizabeth already gave. And Luke says they were all amazed. The mom said it and the dad wrote it, and both land on John.

The answer is praising God. Immediately his mouth is opened and his tongue is released, and Zechariah begins to speak, praising God. Think about that, bakers. After all that silence, the first thing out of his mouth is praise. I think that tells you where his heart was.

The answer is what will this child become. All who heard this wondered in their hearts and asked, “What then will this child become?” They can tell something unusual is going on. And Luke adds that the Lord's hand was with him. The people are curious and the text gives them a reason to be.

The answer is True. Luke says it plainly: “For the Lord’s hand was with him.” That's what he says right after people ask what this child will become. The text gives that as a fact about John. Nobody had to guess.

The answer is that He has visited and redeemed His people. Zechariah, the baby's father, says, “Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, because He has visited and redeemed His people.” That's his reason for the blessing. I can relate, friends. When someone has come and gotten you out of the dark, praise comes easy.

The answer is David. Zechariah says, “He has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of His servant David…” David was Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3). So Zechariah ties this salvation to David's house. That's a big hint about where it's coming from.

The answer is False. Zechariah says God raised up this salvation “…as He spoke through His holy prophets, those of ages past…” The prophets spoke of it long before. What's happening now is what they said was coming.

The answer is Abraham. Zechariah says it's “…the oath He swore to our father Abraham…” Abraham is the man he calls the father of his people. So God's holy covenant goes way back, and Zechariah says God remembers it.

The answer is without fear. Zechariah says God grants deliverance from hostile hands, “…that we may serve Him without fear…” That's a big deal for people who've been under pressure. Serving Him without fear means doing it with no dread hanging over them.

The answer is True. Zechariah says they will serve Him “…in holiness and righteousness before Him all the days of our lives.” Notice how long that lasts, bakers. It's all the days of their lives, not just on the good ones. That's a long stretch of faithful serving.

The answer is to prepare the way for Him. Zechariah tells his son, “…you will go on before the Lord to prepare the way for Him…” John's part is to go first and get the way ready. He doesn't take over the main event. I think there's a lot of honor in that kind of job.

The answer is True. Zechariah says John will give God's people “…the knowledge of salvation through the forgiveness of their sins…” So the knowledge and the forgiveness go together in his words. That's the message John carries.

The answer is those who live in darkness. Zechariah says the Dawn will visit “…to shine on those who live in darkness and in the shadow of death…” Back in the junk drawer I got called out of, friends, one slice of kitchen light meant the whole world to me. So this Dawn is meant for people sitting in the dark.

The answer is wilderness. Luke says the child grew and became strong in spirit, and that he “…lived in the wilderness until the time of his public appearance to Israel.” So the wilderness is the place the verse gives for those years. After that comes his public appearance to Israel. And this story isn't over, bakers.
